elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Retained language: "no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate" — Customer may assign to an affiliate without approval, subject to the pre-existing "financially responsible" qualifier (favourable existing language left intact).

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate or, upon written notice to the other party, to a successor in interest." No consent is required; notice only. "Successor in interest" is generic rather than enumerating merger/acquisition/sale of substantially all assets, but it operates as a consent-free successor carve-out.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The clause is mutual and the new carve-out is mutual ("the other party"), so Vendor may assign without Customer's approval to a financially responsible affiliate or to a successor in interest. To reach preferred, the operative text must make the carve-out Customer-only (e.g., "no such approval shall be required for an assignment by Customer to ...") and leave Vendor assignments wholly subject to Customer's prior written consent.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "without the prior written approval of the other party, which shall not be unreasonably withheld" — applies to the approval Customer must give for a Vendor assignment.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: No competitor bar appears anywhere in the rendered Section 15; add an express prohibition (e.g., "and in no event may Vendor assign to a competitor of Customer").

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise: the record shows no change-of-control provision and no deemed-assignment or termination trigger tied to Customer's change of control, and the edit introduces none, so no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control exists.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: "Neither party shall assign ... except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate or, upon written notice to the other party, to a successor in interest" — the carve-out runs to both parties.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon written notice to the other party, to a successor in interest."
Already met in the original and retained: "Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party."

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Inserted qualifier: "prior written approval of the other party, which shall not be unreasonably withheld."

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the mutual successor carve-out on written notice, the retained consent requirement for other assignments, and the new not-unreasonably-withheld standard all appear in operative language.

Preferred is not reached on two elements: the carve-outs are mutual (so Vendor can assign to an affiliate or successor without Customer's consent), and there is no bar on Vendor assigning to a Customer competitor. These are noted only — the drafter targeted the fallback, which is a permissible landing point.
The change-of-control element is satisfied vacuously: no change-of-control, deemed-assignment, or re-pricing trigger exists in the cited clause or elsewhere in the record, and the edit adds none.

Minimality holds: only two insertions were made ("which shall not be unreasonably withheld" and the successor-on-notice carve-out), the existing affiliate exception and the mutual structure survive verbatim, and no survival tails, procedures, or out-of-checklist requirements were added.

Intent preserved: no defined term is orphaned, no cross-reference dangles, and the retained sentence remains internally consistent — the single sentence now carries one consent standard and two cumulative exceptions.

Finding classification of "deviation" is sound: as drafted, Section 15 had no successor/M&A carve-out (playbook walk-away territory on a merger or sale of substantially all assets) and no reasonableness standard on consent, so it failed the fallback on material terms.
